stem: Who decides to conduct Panchayat elections?

expl: Panchayats (local self-government) are treated as a subject under Entry 5 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. Thus, Panchayat is a State subject. stem: name the Committee which was set up by the nDC in 1957 for the reorganization of CDP and nES, which suggested a three-tier system of rural local government-
expl: For the reorganization of the Community Development Programme (CDP) launched in 1952 and the National Extension Service (NES) launched in 1953, the National Development Council constituted a committee under the chairmanship of Balwant Rai Mehta in 1957. This committee recommended a three-tier Panchayat system (decentralization system) in rural areas—district level, block level and village level.

stem: The Chairman of the Committee set up for the recommendation of Panchayati Raj in India was –
expl: In India, the recommendation to establish a three-tier Panchayati Raj system was made by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957). On the basis of the committee’s recommendations, the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly passed the Panchayati Raj Act in September 1959. In accordance with the provisions of this Act, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated the Panchayati Raj system in Nagaur district of Rajasthan in October 1959. In addition, for reforms in Panchayats, the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977), the G. V. K. Rao Committee (1985) and the Dr. L. M. Singhvi Committee (1986) were also constituted.

stem: What is the main objective of Panchayati Raj?

options.label: c

options.label: d
options.text: Make people capable of participating in development administration

expl: In the Indian context, the basic objective of the Panchayati Raj system is “democratic decentralization with people’s participation.” That is, by taking the process of governance and development down to the village level, to make common people direct participants in decision-making and in the implementation of development programmes.

stem: What is the main characteristic of Panchayati Raj System of Government?

stem: A Panchayat Samiti at the block level is –
expl: At the block level, the Panchayat Samiti is an administrative authority, which functions as a coordinating and supervisory institution between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad (District Panchayat). It establishes a link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zila Parishad. In the Kshetra Panchayat, the elected members will elect from among themselves one Pramukh, one Senior Up-Pramukh, and one Junior Up-Pramukh. The functions assigned to the Kshetra Panchayat will be carried out through committees, and for this purpose the following committees will be constituted— Education Committee, Public Works Committee, Public Health Committee, Family Welfare and Rural Sanitation Committee, etc.

stem: Which Article gives the list of 29 functions to be performed by the Panchayati Raj Institutions?

expl: The list of 29 functions for the Panchayati Raj Institutions is provided under Article 243(G). stem: Which of the following was constituted under the Panchayati Raj system?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Panchayati Raj is a system of democratic decentralization. Provisions related to Panchayats are mentioned in Part IX of the Constitution under Articles 243 to 243-O. In 1957, the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee presented a plan of democratic decentralization and recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. Under this system, there is a Gram Panchayat at the village level, a Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and a Zila Parishad at the district level. Accepting these recommendations, the Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated at Nagaur on 2 October 1959 by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru. It is noteworthy that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. Therefore, the correct option is (c).

stem:
Consider the following statements— After the 73rd Amendment, decentralization was carried out of—
1. Decision-making powers
2. The entire system
3. Judicial powers
4. Administrative powers
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Panchayati Raj is a system created for democratic decentralization. Through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, 16 new Articles were added to Part 9 of the Constitution and the Eleventh Schedule was added. Under this, a total of 29 subjects were placed within the jurisdiction of Panchayats. It is noteworthy that the objective of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is administrative decentralization, not judicial decentralization. After this system came into existence constitutionally, there was no change in the structure of the judiciary in India. Thus, it is clear that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act does not provide a legal basis for judicial decentralization. Administrative powers have also been provided to work in these subjects.

Therefore, the correct answer is (e), i.e., “more than one of the above.”

stem: Which political institution in India has reserved seats for women?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In India, under the Constitution, one-third of the seats are reserved for women at all levels in Panchayati Raj Institutions. In many states, women’s reservation in local bodies has been increased to 50%. At present, through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, one-third of the seats have also been reserved for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. This reservation is to be implemented after delimitation carried out on the basis of the first Census held after 2023. The Constitution mentions that this reservation will be for 15 years.

stem: The legislative origins of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act can be traced back to which Constitutional Amendment Bill?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The statutory beginning of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, which granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions, began with the 64th Constitution (Amendment) Bill. This Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in May 1989 by the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. However, it lapsed because it was not passed by the Rajya Sabha. Thereafter, the 72nd Constitution (Amendment) Bill, 1991 was passed by both Houses of Parliament and was enacted as the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

expl: To review the financial position of Panchayats, the Governor constitutes a Finance Commission at the end of every five years. Under Article 243-I of the Constitution, the Governor has the power to constitute the Finance Commission.

stem: Who is empowered to review financial position of the Panchayats?

options.label: d
options.text: Finance Commission constituted by the Governor

expl: Part IX of the Constitution contains provisions relating to Panchayats. According to Article 243-I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission, which is specifically authorized to review the financial position of Panchayats and to give recommendations to the Governor. This Commission also reviews the financial position of the municipalities of the State under Article 243-Y.

stem: Which of the following functions does not fall under the jurisdiction of local self-government?
expl: Maintenance of public order is not related to local self-government. Maintenance of public order is a subject of the State Government, whereas management of public health and sanitation, roads and bridges, economic and social development planning, fire services, etc., fall under local self-government. Article 243-G deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats, and Article 243-W deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities, etc.
